sentences.text: Xiphactinus was a member of the extinct order Ichthyodectiformes, a group of ancient fish-like reptiles. It superficially resembled a giant, fanged tarpon, though it was not a true tarpon.
This predator grew to a maximum length of 5 to 6 meters, with measurements ranging between 4.3 and 6 meters. It possessed a flat head resembling a bulldog and a relatively thin tail.
The animal had large jaws that likely functioned as a suction tube to catch prey. Its fins were supported by bony rays extending from its body to keep them firm.
A 4.2-meter specimen of X. audax preserved a nearly perfect 1.9-meter ichthyodectid fish named Gillicus arcuatus inside its stomach.
Remains of a Xiphactinus were found inside a large specimen of the shark Cretoxyrhina.
A six-meter-long Xiphactinus specimen found near Morden, Canada, had a mosasaur fin trapped between its jaws.
The genus Xiphactinus was described by Leidy in 1870, following the discovery of the first fossil in the 1850s in the Niobrara Chalk.
Further discoveries included an incomplete skull fossil of a potential new species found in 2002 in the Czech Republic and bones discovered near Morden, Manitoba, in July 2010.
Juvenile teeth suggest that Xiphactinus maintained a fish-eating diet throughout its growth. Its large jaws likely functioned as a suction tube to catch prey.
Xiphactinus likely spent its juvenile stage in shallow seaway margins for protection and food.
Dead or injured Xiphactinus were likely scavenged by sharks such as Cretoxyrhina and Squalicorax.
Xiphactinus fossils range from the Albian to the Maastrichtian stages and are found in Cretaceous formations across the US East Coast, Europe, Australia, Canada, Venezuela, and Argentina.
The species lived in the south and southwest of the United States.
Xiphactinus species and other ichthyodectids went extinct almost at the end of the Late Cretaceous at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.
In popular media, Xiphactinus is depicted in large schools and measures 5 meters, though scientific consensus on these specific behaviors and sizes varies.
